message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, sorted roughly by passenger traffic (largest to smaller but still significant):

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; hub for American Airlines and Delta. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in North America; hub for United Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Hub for American Airlines; one of the largest airports by land area. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver, CO | DEN | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; hub for United and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City, NY | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for many carriers including Delta and JetBlue. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Hub for United and a major gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle, WA | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for international flights to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte, NC | CLT | Hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | Hub for American Airlines; high volume of domestic flights. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando, FL | ORL | Major hub for leisure travel; home to many charter airlines. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark, NJ | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; close proximity to NYC. |
| Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport | Detroit, MI | DTW | Hub for Delta Air Lines; one of the largest airports in the Midwest. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Dulles, VA | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; key airport for the Washington DC metro area. |

These airports serve as major hubs for both domestic and international travel and are often the primary gateways for their respective regions.
